from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Complex numbers are vectors in the plane.",
            "Holomorphic functions map shapes while preserving angles.",
            "Iteration means repeatedly applying the same function."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisites: The Complex Plane and Functions", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show Complex Plane with x and y axes
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], axis_config={"include_numbers": False}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(axes, 'C3')
        self.play(Create(axes), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")

        # Label Real and Imaginary axes
        real_label = Text("Real", font_size=18, color="#FFD700").next_to(axes.x_axis, RIGHT)
        imag_label = Text("Imag", font_size=18, color="#FFD700").next_to(axes.y_axis, UP)
        self.add(real_label, imag_label)

        # Create a point z = a + bi
        z_point = Dot(color="#00FFFF")
        z_pos = axes.c2p(1, 1)
        z_point.move_to(z_pos)
        self.add(z_point)
        self.play(Indicate(z_point), run_time=1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF6347")
        # Placeholder for "preserving angles" visualization
        shape = Square(side_length=0.5, color="#FF6347").scale(0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(shape, 'D4')
        self.play(Create(shape), run_time=1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#90EE90")
        # Show function f(z) = z^2 + c
        func_text = MathTex("f(z) = z^2 + c", color="#FFFFFF", font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(func_text, 'B2')
        self.play(Write(func_text), run_time=1)
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Fixed Points and Attractors", [
            "Fixed points are where the function remains unchanged.",
            "Orbits track a point's movement under repeated iteration.",
            "Stable fixed points attract nearby points like magnets."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        z0 = Dot(point=self.grid["C3"], color=WHITE)
        z0_label = Text("z_0", font_size=18).next_to(z0, UP, buff=0.1)
        self.add(z0, z0_label)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Show orbit trajectory
        dots = VGroup()
        current_pos = self.grid["C3"]
        for i in range(5):
            dot = Dot(point=current_pos, color=BLUE_B).scale(0.8 - i * 0.1)
            dots.add(dot)
            # simulate movement towards attractor
            current_pos = current_pos + np.array([-0.3, 0.1, 0]) 
            self.play(FadeIn(dot))
        
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        attractor = Dot(point=self.grid["C1"], color="#00FF00")
        attractor_label = Text("Attractor", font_size=18, color="#00FF00").next_to(attractor, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(attractor), Write(attractor_label))
        self.wait(3)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Julia sets define boundaries of dynamic behavior.",
            "Small changes lead to vastly different outcomes.",
            "These boundaries form complex, beautiful patterns.",

            "This sensitive dependence creates chaotic boundaries."
        ]

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The Mandelbrot set maps all dynamic possibilities.",
            "It determines if orbits remain bounded or diverge.",
            "It showcases stunning self-similarity at every scale.",
            "Mini-Mandelbrots appear throughout the main structure.",
            "This set acts as the ultimate parameter map."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Mandelbrot Set: The Map of All Dynamics", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        c_plane_label = Text("Parameter c-plane", font_size=24, color=BLUE)
        formula = MathTex(r"f_c(z) = z^2 + c", color=YELLOW)
        mandelbrot_shape = VMobject().set_points_as_corners([
            [-1, 1, 0], [0, 1.5, 0], [1, 1, 0], [1.2, 0, 0], [0.8, -0.5, 0], [0, -1, 0], [-1, -0.5, 0], [-1, 1, 0]
        ]).set_fill(RED, opacity=0.5).set_stroke(WHITE, width=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        self.place_at_grid(c_plane_label, 'A2')
        self.play(Write(c_plane_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'C3')
        self.play(Create(formula))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        self.place_in_area(mandelbrot_shape, 'B4', 'E6')
        self.play(FadeIn(mandelbrot_shape))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[3]))
        # Indicate structure
        self.play(mandelbrot_shape.animate.set_color(PURPLE), run_time=1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[4]))
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(RED),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(PURPLE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(GREEN)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application: Fractal Growth", [
            "Fractals model complex growth in nature.",
            "Recursive rules simulate branching patterns efficiently.",
            "Holomorphic dynamics reveal life's geometric beauty.",
            "Simple rules produce incredible natural complexity.",
            "Mathematics provides a lens to view biology."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        triangle = Triangle(color=BLUE).scale(0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(triangle, 'B3', scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(Create(triangle))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        sub1 = Triangle(color=GREEN).scale(0.25)
        sub2 = Triangle(color=GREEN).scale(0.25)
        sub3 = Triangle(color=GREEN).scale(0.25)
        
        self.place_at_grid(sub1, 'D2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(sub2, 'D4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(sub3, 'E3', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(triangle.copy(), VGroup(sub1, sub2, sub3)))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        # Using a simple recursive-like structure to represent emergence
        emergent = VGroup(*[Star(color=PURPLE, stroke_width=2).scale(0.3) for _ in range(5)])
        emergent.arrange_in_grid(rows=1, cols=5)
        self.place_in_area(emergent, 'C1', 'C6', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(emergent))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.play(emergent.animate.scale(1.5).set_color(PINK))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: Introduction to Holomorphic Dynamics: The Beauty of Iteration
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students in mathematics or physics

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Complex Plane and Functions
sections.content: Review complex numbers as vectors (a + bi) and the concept of a holomorphic function as a mapping that preserves angles (conformal). Define the iteration process: f(f(f(...z...))).
sections.example: Visualizing a point z on the complex plane being 'pushed' by a function f(z) = z².

sections.title: Fixed Points and Attractors
sections.content: Introduce stable and unstable fixed points. Explain the 'Orbit' of a point under iteration. A stable fixed point acts like a gravitational sink.
sections.example: An animation of a 'Digital Magnet' (the fixed point) pulling surrounding scattered particles toward it.

sections.title: The Julia Set: Defining the Boundary of Chaos
sections.content: Explain that the Julia set is the set of points where the dynamic behavior is 'sensitive' or chaotic. Small changes in initial position lead to wildly different long-term orbits.
sections.example: A 'Tug-of-War' visual: Points inside the Julia set flee to infinity, while points outside spiral toward a central attractor.

sections.title: The Mandelbrot Set: The Map of All Dynamics
sections.content: Introduce the Mandelbrot set as the 'parameter space'—a map showing which functions f_c(z) = z² + c produce connected vs. disconnected Julia sets.
sections.example: A zoom-in animation into the Mandelbrot set showing 'mini-Mandelbrot' copies, highlighting self-similarity.

sections.title: Real-World Application: Fractal Growth
sections.content: Connect holomorphic dynamics to nature. Explain how simple recursive rules generate complex structures found in biological systems.
sections.example: A virtual 'Fractal Fern' growing: showing how iterating a simple complex function can simulate the branching patterns of biological life.
